task: Scissors mode B(M1) saturation and valence shell truncation dynamics

primary_papers: Enders et al., Phys. Rev. C 59, R1851 (1999)
Kneissl, Pitz, Zilges, Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys. 37, 349 (1996)
Heyde, von Neumann-Cosel, Richter, Rev. Mod. Phys. 82, 2365 (2010)
evidence_boundaries.mechanistic_law: Establishes that the Scissors Mode B(M1) collectivity does not diverge quadratically as beta2^2, but strictly saturates at a universal quantum ceiling B(M1) ~ 3.0 - 3.4 mu_N^2 across beta2 = 0.25 - 0.35 in rare earths and actinides due to two fundamental microscopic constraints: (1) Valence shell space truncation (closed cores remain inert), and (2) Pairing reduction at large deformation, culminating in complete collapse in superdeformed nuclei (152Dy, B(M1) < 0.5 mu_N^2) where unconstrained macroscopic models overestimate the strength by >29x.
